results.title: 16,000 EBOLA VACCINE DOSES ARRIVE IN CONGO
results.description: KINSHASA, AUGUST 22 /SRNA/ — Congo has received more than 16,000 doses of the Ervebo Ebola vaccine as the country battles what is described as the largest Ebola outbreak in its history, Health Minister Samuel Roger Kamba said. A total of 16,250 doses from an expected shipment of 70,000 arrived last night at the international airport in the capital, Kinshasa. The remaining doses are expected from the World Health Organization /WHO/ and its UN agency partners. Additional doses are expected early next week, AP reported. The current Ebola outbreak in Congo is caused by the rare Bundibugyo virus strain, for which there is currently no approved treatment or vaccine. The virus spreads easily and can go undetected because some of its symptoms are similar to those of other diseases, such as malaria. The Ervebo vaccine is licensed for the prevention of Ebola and has proven effective during previous outbreaks. The WHO said it may also provide some protection against the Bundibugyo virus. According to the latest figures, 2,516 people have died and 5,290 cases of infection have been confirmed since the outbreak began in February. /end/ml/nm

results.title: TRNINIĆ: WILDFIRE SITUATION IMPROVES, TREBINJE STILL HARDEST HIT
results.description: ISTOČNO SARAJEVO, AUGUST 22 /SRNA/ — The wildfire situation in Republika Srpska is slightly better this morning than over the previous two days, while the most difficult situation remains in the Trebinje area, acting director of the Republika Srpska Civil Protection Administration Boris Trninić told SRNA. He noted that fires are also active in Nevesinje, Bileća, Bijeljina, Zvornik and Srebrenica. Although extensive damage has been caused to forests, there has been no damage to buildings and, most importantly, there have been no injuries or fatalities. "I must commend all firefighters in Republika Srpska who have been battling the wildfires for days and making extraordinary efforts to bring them under control," Trninić stressed. He said that at one point around 80 firefighters, a large number of vehicles and a helicopter operated by the Republika Srpska Ministry of Interior's Aviation Unit were deployed in Trebinje. He added that a team from the Republika Srpska Civil Protection Administration had also been deployed to install a water tank and oversee its refilling. A water intake point was positioned as close as possible to the fire in order to reduce the helicopter's flight time. /end/bm/mđ/nm
